reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its main message is a personal cryptocurrency and cloud-mining update that repeatedly warns viewers about pump-and-dump manipulation and urges them to research before spending money. Although the description includes a Crypterra registration link and the speaker discusses his own investment, he presents the service as uncertain, acknowledges that the site was down, and does not make a definite profit or safety promise.

citations.quote: I'm just sharing my own experience in the crypto currency world.
if you wanna save your money do not be a part of pump&dump groups
think twice before you spend your money on anything
i hope it will not be a scam but time will tell
the website was down for the last three days

opening.argument: Judge, the mining-income claim and the requested action appear together. The speaker describes Crypterra as offering two-year mining contracts at attractive prices and says it had been paying out; the description then asks viewers to join through his registration link. That is a pathway from a paid mining product to expected payouts, even though he does not guarantee a return. The risk disclaimer matters, but it does not erase the invitation to register for the same service whose payouts he has described.

citations.quote: it offered like bitcoin or and altcoin mining contracts for two years for great prices compared to hash flow it worked it's been paying out since july 2017
join Crypterra (at your OWN risk! ) https://crypterra.net/?code=CR10953 I would appreciate it if you register through my Links.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense cites his uncertainty and the website outage, but those facts sharpen the concern: he asks viewers to register while acknowledging that the service is unavailable and that he has not recovered his own investment. Warnings about pump-and-dump groups address a different activity; they do not withdraw the Crypterra invitation.

citations.quote: join Crypterra (at your OWN risk! )
the website was down for the last three days
so far, i did not get my investment back

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The link makes this mixed content, but the opening turns a historical payout claim into an implied promise to viewers. The speaker explicitly says he does not know whether Crypterra will return and that his investment has not been recovered. Registration is requested; a dependable return is not promised.

citations.quote: I mean will they really come back? I don't know. Only time will tell but so far, i did not get my investment back
join Crypterra (at your OWN risk! )

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals in combination. The speaker calls Crypterra's two-year mining contracts cheap and says they had paid out. He also reports that its website was down for three days, while the description still provides a join link. His own investment is unrecovered. A favorable account of mining payouts attached to a registration request is especially concerning when the service's availability and the speaker's recovery are unresolved; the caveats disclose those risks, but do not resolve them.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the outage and uncertainty as proof of caution. They are also material reasons to question why the registration link remains alongside favorable payout claims. Saying viewers should research does not establish that the mining contracts are paying now or that an investment can be recovered.

citations.quote: I would appreciate it if you register through my Links.
please do your own research and think twice before you invest or spend your money on anything.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those are genuine risk signals, not evidence that the speaker conceals them or promises a return. He openly reports the outage, says he has not recovered his investment, and leaves the outcome uncertain. His description also tells prospective joiners that the risk is their own.

opening.argument: Judge, the market commentary does not settle the video's role. After discussing coins, the speaker turns to Crypterra, describing low-priced mining contracts and past payouts, then says viewers can see his earlier live purchase. The description asks them to register through his link. His personal-investor framing gives the account an experiential basis, but it also helps steer viewers from hearing about mining income to a way of joining. The criticism of pump-and-dump groups should not make that separate invitation disappear.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that he speaks from experience and warns about manipulation. Neither point makes the Crypterra segment purely informational: he describes past mining payouts, references his own purchase, and leaves viewers a registration route. His doubts qualify the pitch, but they do not remove its promotional effect.
